title: Proposal for relative path support in the table spec
summary: Talat Uyarer and Daniel Weeks proposed relative paths as a V4 table spec change (issue #13141 and a design doc). A dedicated sync was held in July 2025. Wing Yew Poon asked whether a single copy of metadata with several copies of data would be supported; Weeks answered that multiple locations for the same files under one table is explicitly a non-goal and that the open points were about how paths are constructed, resolved and relativized, with all paths made relative to the table location. A January 2026 meeting reached general agreement on the approach. Steve Zhang noted that with relative paths, changing a table's location breaks reads and cleanup of files written under the old location; Weeks replied that relocating data is the responsibility of the catalog or implementation and that absolute paths remain available. Weeks opened spec PR #15630, revised it after review, and in May 2026 changed the design to join the table location and the relative path on the '/' separator, ahead of a planned vote.

positions.stance: Relative paths should be added to the table spec in V4 with a scoped-down proposal.
Inferring the table location from the metadata path does not support one copy of metadata with two or more copies of data.
Multiple copies or locations of the same data files under one table is a non-goal and is better handled by engine or FileIO implementations; all paths should be relative to the table location.
With relative paths a location update is no longer a metadata-only operation, so the spec should acknowledge the behavior change and its effect on snapshot expiration and orphan removal.
How data is relocated when the base location changes is the responsibility of the catalog or implementation, and writers can still produce absolute paths to keep the v1-3 behavior.
The table location and the relative path should be joined on the URI separator '/', which makes relativization unambiguous for similar paths such as 'table' and 'table_v2'.

outcome.note: General agreement on the approach was reported after a January 2026 meeting, and spec PR #15630 is under review. The last message announces a change to separator handling before a vote is sent; no vote appears in this thread.

why_it_matters: With relative paths, changing a table location no longer leaves old files resolvable, so relocation has to move or copy the whole table.
